line_text: L120: **Locus-designator heads.** A disease-denoting premodifier (a spelled-out disease name, or an acronym that the document has already defined as a disease) in attributive position within a noun phrase whose head denotes a gene or locus is a **Modifier**. A locus head is "gene," "genes," or "gene" followed by a numeral or symbol. This rule extends the adjacency test above; it does not restrict it to gene heads. The locus head does not turn the disease span into O. The locus designator and any bare gene symbol remain O. Gene symbols stay outside the schema, and the Specific Disease / Disease Class boundaries are unchanged for non-attributive uses.
